Issue: No canonical tags on any page
Evidence: 0 of 17 pages had rel=canonical. With cleanUrls on, every page was reachable at both /page and /page.html with nothing telling Google which to keep.
Fix: Added a self-referencing canonical to all 17 pages, always on the apex https://www.homemadebycolleen.com host. Home points at the bare domain.
Dev Notes: Verified: 17 of 17 pages now return exactly one canonical. See evidence/static-after.txt.

Issue: No Open Graph or Twitter card tags
Evidence: 0 of 17 pages. Any share on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp or iMessage would show no image and a guessed title.
Fix: Added og:type, og:site_name, og:locale, og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image, og:image:alt plus twitter:card (summary_large_image), twitter:title, twitter:description and twitter:image. Each page gets a relevant photo rather than one shared default.
Dev Notes: 8 og tags and 4 twitter tags per page, measured. Blog posts use og:type=article, everything else website.

Issue: No structured data anywhere on the site
Evidence: 0 of 17 pages had JSON-LD. The live WordPress site gets Organization and WebSite from Rank Math, so the rebuild was a regression against production.
Fix: Added one @graph per page: FoodEstablishment plus LocalBusiness (NAP, phone, logo, sameAs, areaServed for all 8 towns, opening hours), WebSite, WebPage, Article on the 2 blog posts with Colleen Walsh as author, FAQPage where a real FAQ exists, and Service on the 9 service pages.
Dev Notes: All 17 blocks parse as valid JSON and carry every required property for their type. Opening hours came from the footer, not invented. BreadcrumbList deliberately omitted: AGENTS.md bans breadcrumbs sitewide, and breadcrumb schema without a visible trail is a mismatch.

Issue: Every indexed WordPress URL would have 404'd on launch
Evidence: The sitemaps shipped 20 WordPress URLs. 14 pointed at nested paths the flat build does not serve (/service-areas/... and /about-us/...), and 5 had no file at all. No redirects existed: vercel.json contained only cleanUrls.
Fix: Added 15 permanent 301s in vercel.json covering the 8 service-area pages, contact, reviews, meet-the-team, both dated blog post URLs, the category archive and /cater.
Dev Notes: This was the highest-risk item in the build. Confirm against the GSC Pages report before launch and resubmit the sitemap on launch day.

Issue: Sitemaps listed URLs the build does not serve
Evidence: page-sitemap.xml, post-sitemap.xml and category-sitemap.xml were a straight mirror of the WordPress sitemap. Only 1 of 20 URLs (the home page) resolved to a real file.
Fix: Regenerated page-sitemap.xml (15 URLs) and post-sitemap.xml (2 URLs) from the actual built files with priorities, rebuilt sitemap_index.xml, and deleted category-sitemap.xml because the category archive has no page in this build.
Dev Notes: Validated: 17 of 17 sitemap URLs resolve to a built file, 0 broken. All three files parse as well-formed XML.

Issue: No 404 page
Evidence: No 404.html existed, so a bad URL fell through to the Vercel default error page with no branding and no way back into the site.
Fix: Built 404.html on the real site chrome so it inherits the design system. Carries noindex,follow, a primary menu CTA, a home link and six recovery links.
Dev Notes: See evidence/E3-404-page.png. Removed the aria-current it inherited from its source page so no nav item is falsely marked current.

Issue: Preview deployments were fully indexable
Evidence: robots.txt allows everything and no host-scoped noindex existed, so any *.vercel.app preview was a crawlable duplicate of production.
Fix: Added an X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow header in vercel.json scoped with a host condition to *.vercel.app. Production is unaffected.
Dev Notes: Belt and braces: also turn on Vercel Deployment Protection for preview domains. The header alone does not stop a human opening the URL.

Issue: Working files were being deployed
Evidence: The repo root shipped as-is. The 15 KB audit CSV and 1.7 MB of unreferenced images (home-made-logo.png at 1.3 MB, favicon-src.png, 3 unused flower SVGs, 3 unused photos) were all reachable URLs.
Fix: Extended .vercelignore to exclude *.csv and all 8 unreferenced assets. scrape/ and AGENTS.md were already excluded.
Dev Notes: Files stay in the repo for reference, they just stop being served. Cuts roughly 1.7 MB from the deployment.

Issue: Dead Redeem coupon button on the home page
Evidence: index.html carried a primary CTA with href="#". The $15 off block is the main conversion path on the page and the button went nowhere.
Fix: Repointed it at the Prado ordering menu, matching the other order CTAs, with target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer.
Dev Notes: Worth a second look from the business: a coupon button that jumps straight to the menu may want a code shown first.

Issue: 51 dead social links in the footer
Evidence: Every page footer had GoogleFacebookInstagram. 3 dead links on each of 17 pages.
Fix: Repointed to the real profiles found in the WordPress source: the Google share link already used by the reviews CTA, facebook.com/homemadebycolleen/ and instagram.com/homemade_by_colleen/. All open in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer.
Dev Notes: URLs were taken from the scraped live site, not guessed. Same profiles are referenced as sameAs in the schema.

Issue: Two blog titles far over 60 characters
Evidence: 129 and 124 characters. Both repeated the full site name after the real title, so the keyword was pushed past the cut-off in search results.
Fix: Trimmed to 56 and 51 characters by dropping the duplicated brand suffix, which og:site_name already carries.
Dev Notes: about-us.html sits at 61 characters. Left as is: it is one character over and the keywords earn it.

Issue: Meta description too short on one service area page
Evidence: Bridgeville ran 78 characters while its 7 sibling pages ran 135 to 147.
Fix: Rewritten to 142 characters following the exact pattern of the sibling pages.
Dev Notes: blog.html (109), reviews.html (111) and contact-us.html (115) are short but inside tolerance and read well. Left alone deliberately.

Issue: Address did not match itself between header and footer
Evidence: The utility bar on all 17 pages read "300 Mt Lebanon Blvd, Pittsburgh, PA 15234" while the footer read "300 Mt. Lebanon Blvd, Suite 2216-B, Pittsburgh, PA, 15234". Different punctuation and a missing suite number.
Fix: Unified the utility bar to the full footer form including the suite. The same string is now used in the LocalBusiness schema.
Dev Notes: Match this exactly in Google Business Profile and in every citation. NAP consistency is the whole point.

Issue: Opening hours existed on the page but not in schema
Evidence: The footer lists Monday to Friday 9AM to 8PM and Saturday to Sunday 9AM to 4PM on all 17 pages. None of it was machine readable.
Fix: Added openingHoursSpecification to the LocalBusiness node on all 17 pages, taken verbatim from the footer.
Dev Notes: Confirm the hours are still accurate before launch.

Issue: No main landmark on any page
Evidence: 0 of 17 pages had a <main> element. Screen reader users had no way to jump past the utility bar and nav.
Fix: Wrapped the content between </header> and <footer> in <main id="main"> on every page.
Dev Notes: Verified in the rendered DOM: exactly one main#main per page across all 18 pages including the new 404.

Issue: No skip to content link
Evidence: Keyboard users had to tab through the utility bar and all 9 nav items on every page before reaching content.
Fix: Added a skip link as the first focusable element, styled in the design system (yellow fill, 3px ink border), off-screen until focused.
Dev Notes: See evidence/E1-skip-link-focused.png: captured after a single Tab press on the home page.

Issue: Dropdown menus never announced their state
Evidence: Both nav dropdowns (Delivery areas, About us) opened on hover and focus in CSS only. No aria-expanded, no aria-haspopup, so a screen reader was never told a menu had opened.
Fix: Added aria-haspopup and aria-expanded to both triggers on every page, plus a small script that mirrors the CSS hover and focus state into aria-expanded and closes the menu on Escape.
Dev Notes: Tested live, not just in markup: driving mouseenter flips the attribute false to true and mouseleave returns it to false on all 18 pages. See evidence/E2-dropdown-aria-expanded.png.

Issue: Tap targets under the 24px minimum
Evidence: Measured at 390px wide: 4 to 8 undersized targets per page. Utility bar links at 23px tall, footer phone and email at 19px, table-of-contents links at 21px.
Fix: Grew the hit area to 44px on the utility bar, footer contact and social links using a pseudo-element, so the visual design and layout are untouched. Added block padding to table-of-contents and 404 link lists.
Dev Notes: Links inside running sentences were left alone on purpose: WCAG 2.5.8 exempts them. Re-measured: 0 undersized standalone targets across all 18 pages.

Issue: Almost no image lazy loading
Evidence: 16 of 231 image tags had loading=lazy. Every page loaded its full image payload up front.
Fix: Added loading=lazy and decoding=async to 171 below-the-fold images. The logo and the hero on each page stay eager so the LCP element is never deferred.
Dev Notes: Now 197 lazy and 34 eager across 231 tags. The 34 are the per-page logo and hero.

Issue: No cache policy on static assets
Evidence: vercel.json set only cleanUrls, so hashed-free assets in build-assets/ were served with default caching.
Fix: Added Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable for /build-assets/*.
Dev Notes: Filenames are not content-hashed, so bump a filename when an image is replaced or the old one will be served for a year.

Issue: No security headers
Evidence: No X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options or HSTS on any response.
Fix: Added all four sitewide in vercel.json.
Dev Notes: HSTS is set with preload. Only submit the domain to the preload list once you are sure every subdomain is HTTPS.

Issue: Copyright year was stale
Evidence: Every footer read "2025 Homemade By Colleen". It is now late 2026.
Fix: Updated to 2026 on all 17 pages.
Dev Notes: Worth automating at build time so this does not come back every January.

Issue: No analytics, no tag manager, no pixel
Evidence: 0 of 17 pages fire any tracking. The live WordPress site runs Google Site Kit and a Meta pixel today, so launching as-is loses all measurement.
Fix: Add a GTM container sitewide with GA4 and the Meta pixel inside it. Verify that pageviews and outbound clicks to the Prado ordering menu fire before launch.
Dev Notes: NOT DONE and not doable from here: this needs the real GA4 measurement ID, GTM container ID and Meta pixel ID. Nothing was invented. Send the three IDs and this is a 20 minute job.

Issue: Every form on the site is a dead end
Evidence: 18 forms across 17 pages carry onsubmit="return false": the newsletter signup on every page plus the contact form on contact-us.html. A visitor fills them in, nothing is sent, and nobody is notified.
Fix: Wire both to a real endpoint and add a success and an error state, then confirm a test submission lands.
Dev Notes: NOT DONE and not doable from here: needs a decision on the form backend (Formspree, Vercel function, the existing Gravity Forms install or the newsletter provider). Inventing an endpoint would have silently dropped real leads, which is worse than the current visible no-op.

Issue: FAQ on only 3 of 17 pages
Evidence: Real FAQ blocks exist on the home page, the how-it-works page and the Mt. Lebanon area page. The other 7 service area pages have none, so they carry no FAQPage schema either.
Fix: Write 4 to 6 FAQs per area page, phrased as the questions people type into Google and ChatGPT. The FAQPage schema then attaches automatically, since the generator reads the real markup.
Dev Notes: NOT DONE on purpose. I checked the scraped WordPress source: those 7 pages genuinely have no FAQ content to port. AGENTS.md rule 1.4 forbids inventing content, so this needs Colleen or the SEO writer.

Issue: No catering page although /cater/ is indexed
Evidence: The live WordPress site has a /cater/ page with its own content. The rebuild has no equivalent, so the URL had no destination.
Fix: A 301 to /contact-us is in place so the URL is not a dead end. The real fix is porting the catering content to a dedicated page and repointing the redirect.
Dev Notes: The redirect is live and verified. Flagging the content gap rather than silently treating a redirect to contact as a finished page: redirecting content to a contact form is a soft-404 signal to Google.

Issue: aggregateRating deliberately left out
Evidence: reviews.html says "45+ reviews" and the utility bar says "Rated: 5.0". Both are approximate.
Fix: Once the exact review count and average are confirmed in Google Business Profile, add aggregateRating to the LocalBusiness node.
Dev Notes: NOT DONE on purpose. An approximate or inflated review count in schema risks a manual action. I would rather ship without it than ship a number I cannot verify.

Issue: Checked: no em dashes anywhere
Evidence: AGENTS.md rule 1.1 bans U+2014 sitewide. Ran the project's own grep across html, css, js and md excluding scrape/ and .git.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: 0 matches, before and after all edits. The new 404 page and all added comments were written to the same rule.

Issue: Checked: no broken internal links
Evidence: 689 internal href targets resolved against the filesystem.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: 0 broken, re-run after every edit in this pass including the new 404 page.

Issue: Checked: no horizontal overflow on mobile
Evidence: Rendered all 18 pages in headless Chrome at 390px and compared scrollWidth against clientWidth.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: 0px overflow on every page. See evidence/E4-mobile-home.png.

Issue: Checked: content is visible without JavaScript
Evidence: The .reveal animation is already gated behind a .js class set by an inline script, so it cannot hide content when JS fails. Verified by rendering with JavaScript disabled: 0 of 43 reveal elements were hidden and the page measured 10946px tall.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: This was a real P2 defect on the reference site. This build already does it correctly. See evidence/E5-no-js-content-visible.png.

Issue: Checked: all images have alt text and dimensions
Evidence: 231 image tags across 18 pages: 0 missing alt, 0 missing width or height.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: Layout shift risk from images is therefore low. Measured in the rendered DOM, not from the markup.

Issue: Checked: exactly one H1 per page
Evidence: 18 of 18 pages have a single H1. No duplicate or keyword-stuffed H2 patterns found.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: Service area pages run 1,896 to 2,226 words and blog posts 3,089 to 3,744. No thin pages.

Issue: Checked: no JavaScript errors and no failed requests
Evidence: Captured console errors, page errors and failed requests on all 18 pages at mobile and desktop widths.
Fix: No action needed.
Dev Notes: 0 errors and 0 failed requests, including after the nav ARIA script was added.

Issue: Checked: outbound links are safe
Evidence: Every target=_blank link already carried rel=noopener noreferrer, including the ones added in this pass.
Fix: No action needed.

Issue: Absolute internal links with a trailing slash
Evidence: 5 CTA buttons on blog-fresh-local-ingredients used href="https://www.homemadebycolleen.com/meal-prep-delivery-service/" and .../about-us/. Absolute plus a trailing slash: broken when the file is opened locally, and an extra 308 hop in production because trailingSlash is off.
Fix: Repointed all 5 to relative file paths, per AGENTS.md section 4.
Dev Notes: Found by the Broken Links sweep, not visible in the earlier pass. Re-checked: 694 internal links, 0 broken, 0 absolute internal links left in body copy.

Issue: Ordering menu URL used two different casings
Evidence: 52 links pointed at getprado.com/menu and 46 at getprado.com/Menu. Both return 200 today, so nothing was broken, but it is two URLs for one destination.
Fix: Normalised all 98 to the capitalised /Menu form used by the nav CTA.
Dev Notes: Verified with live HTTP requests before changing anything: both variants returned 200, so this was consistency rather than a defect.

Issue: Blog posts are nearly orphaned
Evidence: Both posts have only 2 inbound internal links each, from the blog index and each other. Every other page has 17. Service pages never link to the posts.
Fix: Add a contextual link from each service area page to the relevant post, and a related reading block at the end of each post.
Dev Notes: NOT DONE: this is editorial placement, not a mechanical fix. Dropping links in automatically would put them in the wrong place in the copy. Full inbound and outbound counts are in the Page Inventory tab.

Issue: External links had never been verified
Evidence: 29 distinct external targets across the site, none previously checked.
Fix: Checked each one with a live HTTP request. Ordering menu, Instagram, Google Maps and Google Fonts all return 200. The Google reviews shortlink returns 302 and resolves to the correct Business Profile panel.
Dev Notes: One exception: facebook.com/homemadebycolleen/ returns 400 to every automated request, which is Facebook bot protection rather than evidence of a broken link. It could not be verified here and needs a manual check in a browser. Reported rather than guessed.

Issue: URL structure had never been assessed
Evidence: The rebuild silently changed 14 of 20 indexed URLs by flattening the WordPress folder structure, with no analysis of whether that was the right call.
Fix: Audited all 18 URLs: depth, slug length, keyword placement and redundant tokens. Full analysis in the URL Structure tab.
Dev Notes: Conclusion: keep the current URLs. The 8 service area slugs repeat meal-prep-delivery-service and pennsylvania, and /service-areas/<town>/ would be cleaner, but these URLs are already indexed in their current form and the 301s are live. Changing them twice in one redesign doubles the risk for a marginal gain. AGENTS.md section 4 also mandates flat files with relative links, so nesting would break local navigation. Revisit after 90 days if the cluster underperforms.
